actor: Runtime author and Metal kernel maintainer, Swiftlet project
job: Turning the August publication into something an outsider can install and rerun — documented cache-budget flag, reproducible build, and the settings behind the reported rate.
outcome: A build a third party can run on their own M5 hardware, at a context length and cache budget they choose and can state.
motivation: A runtime whose headline number nobody outside can reproduce is a demo, and the project wants the mechanism judged on its own terms.

task.who: Swiftlet's Swift and Metal runtime author working the public repository
task.what: Document the expert-cache flag and build steps
task.where: The Swiftlet GitHub repository and its README
task.why: Outsiders cannot restate conditions they cannot set
task.how: Command-line cache-budget flag with published build instructions

actor: Independent benchmark author, Apple silicon local-inference testing publication
job: Running the 80-billion-class streamed model across several context lengths and cache budgets, then publishing a table rather than a single throughput figure.
outcome: A published decoding rate for an 80B sparse mixture-of-experts model under expert streaming, stated with the context length it was measured at.
motivation: A number from the party that produced it is the weakest form of benchmark, and rerunning it is the cheapest way to test it.

task.who: Independent testers running local models on their own Apple hardware
task.what: Sweep decoding rate across context and cache settings
task.where: An M5-class Mac running the streaming runtime
task.why: One figure cannot describe a streaming working set
task.how: Repeated timed runs at fixed prompt lengths

actor: Benchmark harness maintainer, open-source local inference benchmarking tool
job: Adding context length and expert-cache budget to the fields a run must report, so a streamed throughput result cannot be published bare.
outcome: A harness whose output carries the conditions alongside the tokens per second, making a condition-stated third-party measurement the default rather than an act of diligence.
motivation: Once weights stream instead of sitting resident, a rate without its working set is not a measurement anyone else can check.

task.who: Maintainers of the harness result schema and reporting output
task.what: Add cache-budget and context fields to results
task.where: The harness result schema and its output format
task.why: Bare rates are unreadable once experts stream
task.how: Versioned result schema with required condition fields

actor: Model release engineering lead, Alibaba Qwen3-Next team
job: Publishing and maintaining the 80-billion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts checkpoints, with the router and expert layout that make streaming from storage viable at all.
outcome: An openly available 80B-class model outside testers can stream on consumer Apple hardware and measure without the runtime author's involvement.
motivation: A sparse model that only its own tooling can run is a model nobody else publishes numbers for.

task.who: Qwen model release and open-weights distribution engineers
task.where: Public model repositories and their conversion tooling
task.why: Outside measurement needs openly available weights
task.how: Sharded safetensors releases with documented expert layout

actor: Framework engineer, Apple MLX machine learning research team
job: Exposing the memory and storage primitives an expert-streaming runtime needs — wired memory limits, mapped weight reads — so a second implementation exists to measure.
outcome: An independent path to run the same model class under streaming, giving outside testers a runtime the original author does not control.
motivation: A framework that only serves resident models cedes the memory-constrained case to whoever is willing to write their own Metal kernels.

task.who: MLX core memory management and model loading engineers
task.what: Expose wired-memory limits and mapped weight loading
task.where: The MLX runtime and its language model library
task.why: A second implementation makes the number checkable
task.how: Memory-mapped weight loading with configurable residency limits

actor: Quantization release engineer, Unsloth GGUF conversion team
job: Shipping the quantized artifacts and a package release for them, so a measured speedup becomes something an outsider can install and time rather than read about.
outcome: Installable quantizations of the model classes involved, with a release users can benchmark independently of the figures the team measured itself.
motivation: The Studio merge shipped a ten-to-twenty-two-times batched-versus-serial rendering figure with no package release to test it against, and that gap invites the same doubt.

task.who: Unsloth quantization and package release engineers
task.what: Cut a package release for the measured build
task.where: The project's GGUF model repositories and release train
task.why: An in-house figure needs an installable artifact
task.how: Tagged releases paired with published quantization recipes

actor: Hardware review editor, Mac silicon review publication
job: Building a local-model section into M5 hardware reviews that reports what a memory-constrained machine actually decodes, at prompt lengths readers recognise.
outcome: A review-desk throughput figure for a streamed 80B-class model on M5 hardware, published with the context length and memory budget it was taken at.
motivation: Unified memory capacity is the buying decision on these machines, and a streamed model is the test that makes the capacity tiers legible.

task.who: Review desk staff running the local inference test suite
task.what: Add streamed large-model decoding to review benchmarks
task.where: The publication's Mac review test bench
task.why: Memory tiers are the reader's actual decision
task.how: Fixed prompt lengths across memory configurations

actor: Local model runtime product manager, desktop LLM application vendor
job: Shipping expert streaming with a user-visible cache budget setting, turning a hand-built runtime trick into something a large installed base runs and reports on.
outcome: A population of users decoding 80B-class models on consumer Macs who can name the cache budget and context length behind whatever rate they see.
motivation: Running a model larger than the machine's memory is what sells a desktop runner, and the setting has to be visible to be supportable.

task.who: Desktop application product and inference backend engineers
task.what: Ship a user-facing expert cache budget control
task.where: The desktop application's model loading settings
task.why: Users can only report settings they can see
task.how: Settings-panel control wired to the streaming backend

actor: Artifact evaluation reviewer, systems and machine learning conference program committee
job: Holding submitted inference throughput claims to stated measurement conditions, so a decoding rate arrives with its context length and residency budget attached.
outcome: Published measurements of streamed sparse models that carry their own conditions, produced by parties with no stake in the runtime being measured.
motivation: A throughput claim without a working set is unreviewable, and the artifact track is where that gets enforced before publication rather than after.

task.who: Artifact evaluation committee members reviewing inference submissions
task.what: Require stated context and residency budget in submissions
task.where: The conference artifact evaluation checklist and reviews
task.why: Unstated conditions make a throughput claim unreviewable
task.how: Artifact checklist requiring reported measurement conditions
